summary: A public e-petition by Adam Samveel asks Parliament to step in over the Bar Council's second amendment to its rules on qualifying law degree programmes. The petition says the amendment changes how exams for these degrees are run from 1 January 2027, with exams held centrally, and that this hits students already partway through their courses. It asks Parliament to consult the relevant authorities so that students who enrolled before the amendment can finish under the old rules.
keyPoints: Affects students in Juris integrated, LLB and other qualifying law degree courses.
The petition argues that changing rules mid-course breaks students' legitimate expectations and legal certainty.
It says working students and those with family duties would face travel and living costs in Malé.
It cites Article 36 of the Constitution (right to education).
Petition reference EPT202600068; referred by the Petition Committee for floor debate.
outcome: Referred by the Petition Committee for debate on the floor; marked completed
